newsitem.title: UK: Hays sees more strength after profits jump.
newsitem.headline: Hays sees more strength after profits jump.

text.p: British distribution and business services company Hays Plc, reporting a 20 percent jump in annual profits said on Monday it had made an encouraging start to the new financial year and was in a strong position. Profits before tax rose to 132.0 million pounds in the year ended June 30 from 110.3 million a year ago, with growth in its all of its main units -- distribution, commercial activities such as document exchange, and personnel operations. "There has been an encouraging start to the new financial year across all the group's operations," executive chairman Ronnie Frost said in the results statement.

"We see considerable opportunities to continue the organic growth in all our activities and to make further complementary acquisitions," he said, adding that Hays had strengthened its management team and was in a strong position.

Hays is paying a final dividend of 5.5 pence, making for a 16 percent rise in the total to 8.1 pence. Earnings per share rose by 19 percent to 22.3 pence. Shares in Hays, which earlier this year made a bid approach to transport company Christian Salvesen Plc but withdrew when no recommendation came from Salvesen directors or support from the Salvesen family, fell two pence after the results to 479.
The fast-growing company since the end of the year end acquired ICS Corp, which provides early morning delivery services, for 65 million pounds.

It said cash generation in the year remained strong in the year, with interest charges covered 20 times by operating profit after spending a net 72 million pounds on acquisitions and capital projects.
